sections.heading: Toyota detail makes this more than the cheapest entry route.
paragraphs: The gray 4Runner is for the buyer who wants a finished Toyota SUV to drive slowly over a small course and display between sessions. Its licensed Pro-Line ABS body and Toyo tire package give a specific reason to choose it over another SCX24. The 132mm wheelbase also makes a different course proposition from the long Gladiator. I would pay for this package when the scale body matters, while a driver planning to discard the body immediately should compare the cost of that whole project first.

sections.heading: The included basket is useful for a first crawler.
paragraphs: Axial supplies the assembled AXI-2035T2, Spektrum SLT2 system, 350mAh 2S pack, USB-C charger and four AA transmitter cells. That reduces the chance of ordering an incompatible battery merely because another micro owner recommends it. Begin with the included equipment, then match any spare against the manual and original pack. The official specification table's USB connector entry is not a clear description of the vehicle battery plug, so inspect the exact connector before ordering an adapter or alternative charging arrangement.

sections.heading: The motor-size discrepancy deserves a visible note.
paragraphs: Axial's product table identifies a 030 brushed motor, while Greg Vogel's RC Driver article calls the motor 050-size. This review does not silently combine those statements into a confident invented specification. The listed official hardware is the primary reference, and the discrepancy belongs in the evidence ledger. The worm-axle drivetrain and single-speed crawling purpose are clear enough to establish the buying case without pretending we have inspected the motor can. If a replacement is needed, check the installed label and model-specific parts drawing.

sections.heading: Proportional controls help you enjoy the body at its intended pace.
paragraphs: The supplied SLT2 offers proportional control and a throttle limiter for learning small approaches. Reduced available output is useful for practice, but it is not a precise reduced-speed specification. RC Driver's 4Runner coverage includes its own running observations; we have not reproduced those runs. For this body-focused purchase, a tight course and smooth inputs are more relevant than maximizing the length of a straight.

sections.heading: Oil damping is useful equipment, and body clearance still matters.
paragraphs: The 4Runner has 6mm oil shocks and a three-link front/four-link rear solid-axle layout in the official description. Damping offers more controlled suspension movement than an undamped spring alone, but it does not remove the effects of body height and weight distribution. Before fitting taller tires or longer shocks, check full steering and articulation clearance with the existing hard shell. Raising the body to cure a tire rub changes more than appearance, so record the original settings and choose one alteration at a time.

sections.heading: The Toyo tires belong on obstacles scaled to the vehicle.
paragraphs: Pro-Line Toyo Open Country R/T Trail tires and Mini Impulse bead-lock wheels provide the stock contact package. They are a specific included feature, not proof of a best-in-class grip result. RC Driver notes limited walking speed and a relatively top-heavy hard-body presentation in its own coverage. Those observations make it sensible to choose tight technical courses rather than long hikes. I would use dry rocks or a clean indoor layout with gradual crests, giving the truck a chance to approach without repeatedly rolling from a sharp edge.

sections.heading: The hinged hard body is both the appeal and the access point.
paragraphs: A finished ABS Toyota shell saves trimming and painting, while the hinged quick-latch arrangement makes routine battery access easier. Check how the body opens before pulling on light leads or forcing a caught wire. RC Driver reports minor wear after its own rolls; that remains a report about its sample, not our body durability rating. Keep the mirrors, latch and mounting hardware under observation after a tumble, and use the exact parts documentation when a cosmetic replacement is required.

sections.heading: Pay for the finished package only if it is the package you want.
paragraphs: The manufacturer reference recorded on 13 October 2026 is $159.99 for this complete 4Runner. The pack, charger and radio cells are included. That is a clear starting purchase for a Toyota-body enthusiast; a driver planning to remove the hard shell or replace the electronics should price that different project first. Tools, spare batteries and tuning pieces have not been priced for this revision, and the old reference is not a current Amazon offer.

sections.heading: The Gladiator offers a longer pickup route.
paragraphs: The green V2 Jeep Gladiator is another complete SCX24 package with a longer published 155mm wheelbase and a polycarbonate pickup body. It is worth considering when the overland bed accessories and longer stance are the desired scale experience. The 4Runner's shorter format and hard Toyota shell give different reasons to choose it. There is no RC Car King head-to-head traction or stability test behind this comparison. Both vehicles should be matched to the obstacle layout and owned as their exact radio and suspension generations.

sections.heading: This is a strong scale-first starter with transparent evidence limits.
paragraphs: The 4Runner has a convincing coordinated purchase for a Toyota fan entering micro crawling. Its body, supplied power equipment, oil damping and model documentation make the startup case clear. The motor-size conflict is a limitation in the published evidence, and it is kept visible instead of repaired by guesswork. I would shortlist it for small technical courses and use the stock configuration before buying changes. Skip it when speed over a long trail, maximum stripped-body performance or a different local class is the actual goal.

faqs.question: What is included with the gray AXI-2035T2?
faqs.answer: The assembled 4Runner, Spektrum SLT2 system, 350mAh 2S LiPo, USB-C charger and four AA transmitter cells are listed in the documented package.

faqs.question: Why are both 030 and 050 motor sizes mentioned?
faqs.answer: Axial’s table specifies 030; Greg Vogel’s RC Driver coverage calls it 050-size. We preserve the disagreement and recommend checking the installed label and parts drawing before replacing it.

faqs.question: Does the USB specification identify the battery plug?
faqs.answer: No. The recorded table’s USB connector entry does not clearly identify the vehicle battery connection. Inspect the original pack and exact manual before ordering an adapter or spare.

faqs.question: How does the body differ from the Gladiator?
faqs.answer: The Toyota has a hinged, quick-latch ABS hard body and a 132mm wheelbase. The Gladiator V2 has a polycarbonate pickup body and a longer published 155mm wheelbase. Body preference and course space are useful comparison points.

faqs.question: Is the 4Runner suitable for long walking trails?
faqs.answer: Its slow micro-crawling purpose and RC Driver’s limited-walking-speed observations favor a short technical course. This review does not recommend buying it as a trail-covering vehicle.

faqs.question: Does the score include a physical rollover or wear test?
faqs.answer: No. The score evaluates the documented buying case for a scale-focused Toyota owner. Outside running observations are attributed, and RC Car King has not measured grip, rollover limits, body wear or runtime.
